statement: When an agent records an operator's ruling in a durable record, quote the operator's words and keep the agent's own reasoning visibly separate. In Cejel #554 the operator replied "a," to a list of options. The first draft put three reasons under the heading "Operator ruling" although the operator gave none, so the record attributed the agent's rationale to the operator. The next draft quoted the chosen option but silently dropped its third sentence, the agent's own proposed fetch-depth: 0 follow-up. Review caught both. Rules: quote the reply verbatim and the chosen option whole, or mark what is left out; label the agent's explanation as not the operator's words and say whether the operator adopted it; do not add forward rules the operator did not make (the first draft said "Any other systematic limit needs its own ruling.").

A claim that a pull request contains no change for something must be checked against the PR's commits, not only its net diff. While preparing alfred #3211's signed closures, a Cejel lesson record was bound to PR #468 ("Land the checked citation relocation with the scoring-fix and paired-result PR."). #468's net diff had no such hunk, so the first write-up told the operator that no hunk in #468 relocated a citation. The relocation had landed inside #468 (commit 8e00f0c42, three line-number moves), and #468's final merge of main replaced it with #464's content-keyed locations, so the net diff showed nothing. The record closed on #464 instead, whose diff carries the hunks. Rules: list the PR's commits before saying a change is absent; when a merge from the base supersedes in-PR work, name the PR whose diff carries the change; evidence read only from a net diff cannot show superseded work.

A record that says a change lands after release X, or keys a reader's inference on toolVersion X, is a claim about merge order, and nothing enforces it. Cejel's release driver tags whatever main's head is, and main reports the version of the latest release prep until the next one, so a build from main after a merge reports the same version as the release. In #560 the first records said a 1.8 report with toolVersion 0.6.8 never carries a new disclosure, and the same draft said v27 "shipped" in 0.6.8 before it was tagged. Rules: gate the merge explicitly in the PR body when records depend on order; never key an absence rule on toolVersion; key it on a format version the change itself bumps, or state only what holds on every report; check that the tag exists before writing that something shipped.
